summary: No candidate. (1) Worst-case uarch cycles of one mcycle: by construction one mcycle runs at most one interrupt delivery plus exactly one instruction (or a fetch fault), with no misaligned-access splitting (misaligned loads/stores trap), page walks of at most 4 levels (Sv57 compiled out by NO_SATP_MODE_SV57), PTE reads only through PMA_RAM_INDEX (no find_pma), and at most two privilege changes, so at most two full TLB flushes (768 ecall writes each). Measured with a bare-metal stress guest (scratch RGUARCH/stress*.S, measure.lua) that stacks, in ONE mcycle, a delegated SSIP interrupt U->S (full flush), a cold 4-level Sv48 fetch walk with A-bit update, an AMO doing a 4-level read walk plus a 4-level write walk that page-faults, and the S->M exception (second full flush), with the AMO target's PMA placed after 8 flash drives so find_pma constructs every mock range: maximum 39,029 uarch cycles (36,053 without the flash drives; csrw satp / sfence.vma / store variants 35,076-35,534), against UARCH_CYCLE_MAX = 1,048,575 (26x margin). Every mcycle halted, and the native interpreter agreed with the uarch root hash. (2) Trap paths compiled into the pristine uarch program (uarch-ram.elf.objdump): the only ebreak sites are abort() and the post-halt __builtin_trap; abort() is called from 11 sites: soft-float i_sfloat32::normalize/normalize2 asserts (shift>=0; proven: add max mantissa < 2^28, fma sum < 2^31), do_read_pma's throw_abort (mock-address-range construction/compat check; PMA table is host-built, read-only to the guest, VirtIO refused in reproducible machines, so only CLINT/PLIC/HTIF/memory/empty entries exist), device_state_access do_read_memory/do_write_memory (only VirtIO calls them), __cxa_pure_virtual (no pure virtual reachable), assert_no_brk x5 (enumerated every change to mip/mie/mideleg/iprv/mstatus.{MIE,SIE}: each returns success_and_serve_interrupts or clears the IE bit via raise_exception; iflags X/Y/H are set only by HTIF paths returning success_and_yield/halt), get_highest_priority_irq_num assert(false) (mip/mie WARL-masked to the six listed bits on read and write), and interpret's final mcycle==effective_mcycle_end assert. Instruction set of the uarch binary: every mnemonic is in SUPPORTED_UARCH_INSN (no fence/mul/compressed). ECALLs: halt, putchar, write_tlb with set<3 and slot<256 by construction. Uarch memory map: the bridge writes only shadow registers the interpreter owns (never x0: every write_x to rd is guarded or rd0-dispatched), uarch-writable memory (protected/host-read-only ranges are never written by the interpreter because W PMAs exclude them), and the TLB via ecall. Uarch stack has ~1.4 MiB free above _end=0x69A328. (3) Differential single-instruction fuzz (fuzz.lua: run_uarch to halt vs native run, root-hash compared, registers set to edge values): every 16-bit encoding in M, S and U mode (3 x 49,152) and 300,000 random 32-bit encodings (180k in M, 60k in S, 60k in U): no uarch failure, no divergence (fuzz.out).
not_covered: Stress measurement used Sv48 with bare-metal guests only; no Linux workload was profiled per mcycle, and no exhaustive search over all instruction/interrupt/trap combinations (the bound rests on the structural argument of at most one interrupt + one instruction + two full flushes + <=3 page walks per mcycle, plus measured costs).

Heaviest FP/integer instructions (fdiv/fsqrt/fma on subnormals, div/rem, mulh on rv64i software arithmetic) were not re-measured in combination with the interrupt+flush stack; earlier measurements (3-4k uarch cycles) plus the structure (an instruction cannot both compute heavily and add a second flush beyond the exception) keep the total under ~45k.

Random 32-bit fuzz ran only with satp=0 (bare) and without CLINT/PLIC/HTIF-specific register setups; it does not exercise page-walk or device paths per instruction (those were covered by the stress guest and by code reading).
Off-chain/Solidity verifier replay of the stress mcycles (log_step_uarch + verify / EVM) was not run; only native uarch vs native interpreter root hashes were compared.
Uarch behavior on non-valid-template states (corrupt TLB, corrupt PMA table, illegal iprv) was not examined beyond confirming they are unreachable (R10 territory).
uarch reset restoring all of uarch RAM (bss guard of the static mock_address_ranges cache) was assumed from earlier reset/pristine-hash checks, not re-verified.
The CODE_COVERAGE uarch build and the ZK interpreter build were not examined.
